messages:
emily-support: Heads-up — ACME reported model behavior changed after today's canary in eu-west. Only seeing it in eu-west-a100-2. They say summaries are truncating facts and code blocks lose formatting. Also seeing occasional 403s for identical requests.

april-cs: adding ticket details — they attached before/after outputs and said it started right after the canary push at ~1866999800. Canary was 20% traffic to eu-west clusters. Model: redwood/gpt-neo-13b-v2 (serving variant v3-quant).

josh-eng: can you paste the minimal repro curl and the two outputs?

emily-support: minimal repro they used (redacted key):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-neo-13b-v2","input":"Summarize: The quarterly revenue grew 12% year-over-year, but product returns increased due to faulty batch X. Explain impact.","max_tokens":80}'
```
Customer-provided outputs:
- before (pre-canary): "The revenue grew 12% YoY. Returns due to batch X increased R% leading to a projected net margin drop of 1.2 points. Recommended: recall batch X, issue patch."
- after (eu-west-a100-2, post-canary): "Revenue grew 12%. Returns mentioned." (truncated, missing the impact analysis and recommendation).

sabrina-qa: quick q — is this only on A100s in eu-west? Do we see same on h100 in ap-sg or eu-central? We pushed a kernel/driver update to eu-west nodes last night.

mike-ops: digging in. eu-west-a100-2 shows nvidia-driver 535.113 and cuBLAS 2.3.4; eu-west-a100-1 (control) has 535.102 and cuBLAS 2.3.2. I also see a runtime patch rolled at 1866999000 where we switched some quant kernels to path B for newer drivers.

josh-eng: that could cause quant-precision parity differences and different token selection. Repro steps for the team: set model_variant=quantized-v3 and run the same curl with header X-Region: eu-west to force routing. Also run without the header to route to default (eu-central). Compare token sequences.

emily-support: note the customer also reported p50 latency spikes during canary window (~350ms -> ~900ms) and intermittent 403s using the same API key for identical requests.

mike-ops: 403 traces correlate with gateway auth timeouts that happened when a worker crashed and restarted. I see OOM/restart events on eu-west-a100-2 around 1867001100 in the runtime logs. Snippet:
```
[1867001100] runtime: OOM killed worker pid=1245 gpu_mem=39GB model=redwood/gpt-neo-13b-v2 quantized
[1867001112] watchdog: restart worker worker-7 (canary)
```
That would explain transient 403s during the spike.

april-cs: customer is asking for ETA and has threatened to pause their integration if behavior persists. They want rollback if no quick fix.

josh-eng: proposed immediate plan:
1) scale canary down to 0% in eu-west (stop the new kernels).
2) pin eu-west-a100 nodes to previous driver/kernel build and roll back the quant kernel change.
3) reproduce locally on a repro VM with driver 535.113 to confirm the parity issue.
4) run token-level diffs on ACME's prompt set and prepare a hotfix or rollback.
Mike — can you scale the canary and repro? Sabrina — start evals on their prompt set.

mike-ops: scaling canary to 0% for eu-west now. Creating repro VM with driver 535.113 and matching cuBLAS. Monitoring OOMs and memory limits.

sabrina-qa: will run the customer's prompt set once the VM is up and post token diff matrix. Also kicking off eval harness comparing eu-west vs eu-central.

deploy-bot: canary config updated: eu-west -> 0% (change_id: dpl_2026_03_17_08)

emily-support: told ACME we scaled canary down and we're investigating; asked for any additional failing prompts. They replied with 6 more examples. Thank you all. :pray:

josh-eng: follow-up action for postmortem — add per-region token-level divergence checks to rollout pipeline and automated rollback if divergence > 0.5% on monitored eval sets. Also add a preflight for driver/kernel mismatches when changing quant kernel codepaths.

mike-ops: auth 403 spikes stopped after canary scale-down. Keeping thread open until we have repro and a fix.

emily-support: keeping customer updated. Closing loop once we ship patch or rollback confirmed in production.
